summary: Deletes unconfirmed subscriptions through garbage collection. Use `before_date` to set the cutoff date for the subscriptions to remove.

Adds or removes subscribers from the blocklist based on an SQL expression or subscriber identifiers. Provide the expression as plain text or use a JSON body to specify `query`, `ids`, and any applicable `action`, `target_list_ids`, or `status` filters.

Deletes subscribers selected by an SQL expression or subscriber identifiers. Provide the expression as plain text or use a JSON body to specify `query`, `ids`, and any applicable `action`, `target_list_ids`, or `status` filters.

Lists statistics for the campaign identified by `campaign_id`. Supply the campaign ID as a number to retrieve its running campaign statistics. The response contains statistics for the requested campaign.
Retrieves logs from an ongoing subscriber import. Use this endpoint to inspect import activity while the import is running.

Adds, removes, or unsubscribes subscribers from lists based on an SQL expression or subscriber identifiers. Provide the expression as plain text or use a JSON body to specify `query`, `ids`, and the applicable `action`, `target_list_ids`, or `status` filters.
Tests SMTP settings using the supplied SMTP configuration values. Provide any settings to test in the request body; all listed fields are optional.
Manages subscribers on the blocklist using subscriber selectors and list settings. Provide `action` to specify whether to add, remove, or unsubscribe the selected subscribers.

Submits a subscription request through the public API. Include `email` and optionally `name` and `list_uuids` in the request body; the schema does not mark any fields as required. A 200 response indicates whether opt-in is required in `has_optin`.
Sends a stop signal to the subscriber importer. Use this endpoint to request that an ongoing import stop.
Retrieves the current status of subscriber imports. Use this endpoint to check the import status without submitting an import request.

Uploads and imports a ZIP file containing one or more CSV files of subscribers. Send the upload as `multipart/form-data`; `params` can contain import settings as a JSON string. Use GET /import/subscribers to retrieve import status.

Manages subscriber membership across lists by adding, removing, or unsubscribing subscribers. Supply `action` and the subscriber or list selectors that define which records to modify; `action` must be `add`, `remove`, or `unsubscribe`.
Generates an HTML preview from the supplied template parameters. Provide `template_type` to identify the template type and `body` to supply the template content.
Returns chart data points for the dashboard. Use the `link_clicks` and `campaign_views` data to render the corresponding dashboard charts.
Returns statistics counts for the dashboard. Use the returned counts to display summary statistics in the dashboard.
Restarts the application. Use this operation to reload the application process and its configuration.
Lists the public mailing lists with their minimal identifying fields. Use this endpoint to retrieve each list's `uuid` and `name` for display or subscription workflows.
Deletes orphaned or blocklisted subscribers through garbage collection. Specify the subscriber category to collect with the `type` path parameter.

Manages the blocklist for the subscriber identified by the path parameter. Use the `id` path parameter to select the subscriber and provide the action and any additional selectors in the request body.
Deletes campaign analytics of the specified type. Use `before_date` to set the date cutoff for the analytics to remove.

Retrieves campaign analytics for the requested statistic type and date range. Use `type` to select links, views, clicks, or bounces, and provide `from`, `to`, and `id` to scope the results. The response contains counts over time for the specified campaign ID or IDs.
Deletes the bounce records associated with a specific subscriber. Supply the subscriber's numeric `id` to identify whose bounce records to delete.
Retrieves bounce records associated with a specific subscriber. Supply the subscriber's numeric `id` to look up the records for that subscriber.
Retrieves a subscriber's profile and related activity data for export. Supply the subscriber's numeric `id` to retrieve profile details, subscriptions, campaign views, and link clicks.
Replaces the archive settings for a campaign. Use `archive` to set the archive state and `archive_template_id` or `archive_meta` to provide related archive configuration.
Submits updated content for a campaign and converts it to the campaign's content format. Use the campaign identifier in the path and provide any campaign content fields you want to submit.
Retrieves the rendered HTML preview of a campaign's body. Supply the campaign's integer `id` to select the campaign whose preview you want to view.

summary: Renders an HTML preview of a campaign using the supplied template and content fields. Use `id` to identify the campaign and provide the preview inputs as form-encoded fields. The request body fields are optional in the schema.

responseModes.example:
Hi John!

This is a e-mail campaign. Your second name is Doe and you are from Bengaluru

summary: Sends an opt-in confirmation email to a subscriber. Supply the subscriber's numeric `id` to identify the recipient of the confirmation email.

Manages subscriber membership in a specified list by adding, removing, or unsubscribing subscribers. Use the `id` path parameter to select the list and provide the subscriber selectors and `action` in the request body.
Sets the specified template as the default template. Use the template's integer identifier to select which template to make the default.
Renders an HTML preview for a template identified by its integer ID. Supply `template_type` and `body` as form-encoded preview parameters.
Replaces the status of a campaign. Set `status` to `scheduled`, `running`, `paused`, or `cancelled` when you want to change the campaign's state.
Submits a test campaign message to selected subscribers. Provide the campaign identifier and a request body with the test message configuration; the body can use JSON or form-encoded data.

Renders a text preview of a campaign using the supplied template and content fields. Use `id` to identify the campaign and provide the preview inputs as form-encoded fields. The request body fields are optional in the schema.

responseModes.example:
Hi John!

This is a test e-mail campaign. Your second name is Doe and you are from Bengaluru

summary: Deletes one or more subscribers identified by the `id` query parameter. Supply the subscriber ID or IDs as a string, with each ID identifying a subscriber to delete.

Lists subscribers, with options to filter and sort the results. Use `query` to filter with an SQL expression, `list_id` to filter by lists, and `order_by` and `order` to control sorting. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.

Creates a subscriber from the supplied subscriber details. The request body may be omitted, and no fields are required by the schema; include values such as `email`, `name`, or `lists` to set subscriber data.

Lists campaigns, with optional filters for status and tags and optional sorting controls. Use `query` to apply custom SQL criteria, or use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results. Set `no_body` to true to request a response without body content.

Creates a campaign from the campaign details supplied in the request body. Provide fields such as `name`, `subject`, and `lists` to define the campaign; all body fields are optional in the schema. A successful response contains the new campaign object.
Lists templates. Set `no_body` to control whether template bodies are included in the response.
Creates a new template. Supply `name`, `type`, and `body`; choose `type` from `campaign`, `campaign_visual`, or `tx`, and include `subject` or `body_source` when relevant to that template type.
Returns the settings stored in the database. Use this endpoint to retrieve the server's current configuration settings.
Updates settings stored in the database. Supply the settings fields you want to update; each listed field is optional.
Deletes bounce records selected by a deletion flag or bounce identifiers. Use `all` to indicate bulk deletion or `id` to provide the bounce identifiers to delete.

Lists bounce records, optionally filtered by campaign or source and sorted by a selected field. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results; set `per_page` to `all` to retrieve all results without pagination.
Returns the general server configuration. Use this endpoint to retrieve the configuration object exposed by the server.
Returns the service health-check result. Use the boolean `data` value to determine whether the service is responding.

Lists mailing lists with metadata such as subscriber counts. Use `query` to search by list name, `tag` to filter by tags, and `order_by` and `order` to control sorting. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.

Creates a mailing list from the supplied list details. Provide `name`, `type`, `optin`, `tags`, or `description` as needed; `type` and `optin` have defined accepted values. The response includes the created list and its metadata.
Lists uploaded media. Use this endpoint to retrieve the available media records and their file details.
Uploads a media file. Send the file as a binary value using `multipart/form-data`; the request body schema does not define additional metadata fields.
Lists log entries currently stored in the log buffer. Use this endpoint to retrieve the buffered entries as an array of strings.
Sends a transactional message to a subscriber. Use `subscriber_email` or `subscriber_id` to identify the recipient, and provide message content or a `template_id` as needed.
Deletes a subscriber identified by its path parameter. Use the subscriber's integer `id` to select the record to remove.
Retrieves a subscriber by its identifier. Use the `id` path parameter to select the subscriber whose details you want to view.

Replaces subscriber data for the subscriber identified by the path parameter. The request body may be omitted, and the schema does not require any fields; supply the subscriber properties you want included in the update.
Deletes the campaign identified by `id`. Use the campaign's integer identifier to select the campaign to remove. The response contains a boolean result.
Retrieves a campaign by its identifier. Use `id` to select the campaign, and set `no_body` to true if you want the response without body content.

Replaces campaign details for the campaign identified by `id`. Supply the campaign fields you want to set, such as `name`, `subject`, or `lists`; the schema does not require any particular body fields. A successful response contains the updated campaign object.
Deletes a template by its identifier. Use this operation when you no longer need the template; the response indicates whether the deletion succeeded.
Retrieves a template by its identifier. Use the `no_body` query parameter to request a response with or without the template body.
Replaces a template's configuration. Supply the template properties you want to set, and use `type` to choose campaign, visual campaign, or transactional template behavior.
Deletes a single bounce identified by its ID in the URI. Supply the integer `id` of the bounce you want to remove.
Retrieves a bounce record by its identifier. Supply the record's numeric `id` to look up the bounce you want to retrieve.
Deletes a mailing list identified by its ID in the URI. Supply the list's integer `list_id` to specify which list to remove.
Retrieves a mailing list with metadata such as its subscriber count. Supply the list's integer `list_id` to identify the list to retrieve.
Replaces the supplied fields on a mailing list identified by its ID. The request body can include list settings, tags, and metadata; all body fields are optional in the schema.
Deletes an uploaded media record. Supply the media identifier for the record you want to remove.
Retrieves an uploaded media record by its identifier. Use the media identifier to access the record's file details and URLs.
Returns the JSON language pack for the requested language code. Supply `lang` to select the language pack to retrieve.
